clue.text: New York landmark could be quite a mess — that's about right!

indicators.note: 'about' means the messed-up letters sit around the next abbreviation
'could be' says the letters might form something else once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters of fodder
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tourist grumbles that a famous New York spot is really rather messy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'quite a mess' is fodder, rearranged with R tucked among its letters to give TIMES SQUARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Times Square is the famous Manhattan intersection known for neon billboards and New Year celebrations.

clue.text: Driving manoeuvres go into possible speeding penalty

indicators.note: 'go into' places the word for go inside the penalty phrase

parts.note: a UK speeding offence typically adds three points to a driving licence
a go or turn in a game

explanation.surface: A driving instructor warns that certain manoeuvres could land you with a speeding penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, offences add penalty points to your licence; TURN goes between the T and S of THREE POINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-point turn reverses a car's direction in a narrow road using forward, back and forward moves.

clue.text: Chicken may be stuffed with lemon finally, as intended

indicators.note: a stuffed bird has its filling inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: chicken is one example of meat

indicators.note: 'finally' keeps only the closing letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the final letter of lemon

explanation.surface: A recipe note: the roast chicken is meant to be stuffed with lemon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken may be' defines by example: chicken is a kind of MEAT, which takes N inside to make MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant and intended both describe something done on purpose or planned in advance.

clue.text: Smelly strongish cheese (Emmental not Taleggio) excites diners for starters

indicators.note: starters are the first course, so each word contributes its opening letter

parts.words: strongish cheese (Emmental not Taleggio) excites diners
parts.note: the initial letters of seven consecutive words

explanation.surface: A cheeseboard verdict: a pungent cheese delights diners, though it's the Emmental rather than the Taleggio.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the words after 'Smelly' are used; 'Smelly' itself is the definition, even though its S looks as if it should start the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Scented means having a noticeable odour, so it can stand for smelly, though usually more pleasantly.

clue.text: Falling out could produce equal rights

indicators.note: 'could produce' says the letters can be turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for right, so two rights are RR

explanation.surface: A wry comment that a row could break out over equal rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'rights' gives two Rs, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out is a disagreement or argument between people, which is what a quarrel is.

clue.text: Ridiculous cut bad editor's taken

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so the following words get jumbled

parts.note: these six letters rearranged
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A writer complains about an absurd cut the poor editor has made.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abducted is to be carried off or kidnapped, so a person taken by force has been abducted.

clue.text: Devouring autobiography and taking it back

parts.note: devouring is eating greedily
an autobiography is written in the author's own words

explanation.surface: Someone gobbles up a memoir, then retracts what they said about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The image of literally eating a book makes the idiom vivid: an autobiography is one's words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating one's words is the idiom for retracting a statement and admitting it was wrong.

clue.text: Someone who badly treats bear wandering around America

indicators.note: wandering things drift out of place, so the letters of the animal shift about
'around' wraps the rearranged letters about the country's abbreviation

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
US is the standard short form of America

explanation.surface: A dancing bear is mistreated as it is taken on a tour of America.
explanation.definitionFit: An abuser is a person who mistreats or harms another, defined here by a descriptive phrase.

clue.text: Begins to tell jokes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in ... on with a job or ... open a bottle, starting it

explanation.surface: A comedian launches into the routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, 'begins to tell jokes', but it splits at 'to', which joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally to crack on means to start, and to crack a joke means to tell one.

clue.text: Pub anger produces fire

parts.note: a bar is a pub
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Tempers flare in a pub, leading to a furious outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a verb or a blaze, but it is the noun for artillery shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a concentrated burst of artillery fire laid down over an area.

clue.text: Book reviewer half shut radio broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order
'half' means only two of the four letters of the following word survive

parts.note: the back half of this word is kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: A literary critic's radio broadcast is half shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book reviewer' suggests a literary critic, but the books are accounts: the second half of SHUT, UT, joins RADIO in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines an organisation's financial books, checking that its accounts are accurate.

clue.text: Observer magazine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who watches an event
second meaning: The ..., a long-running British weekly political magazine

explanation.walkthrough: The capital O suggests The Observer, a British Sunday newspaper, but here it is a plain onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches an event, and The Spectator is a British current affairs weekly.

clue.text: Fancy niche accommodation for sceptic

indicators.note: accommodation houses something, so the phrase before it gives lodging to a word

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An estate agent advertises a stylish little nook as housing for a doubter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer is sitting in fanCY NICHe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic doubts people's motives and claims, much as a sceptic questions accepted beliefs.

clue.text: See 19
Saluted our strange type of relationship

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such a relationship

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd and out of shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: ten letters of fodder taken together

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the way we greeted each other hinted at something odd between us.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterous relationship is an affair involving a married person and someone other than their spouse.

clue.text: Huge performance trick

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
an antic is a playful trick or caper

explanation.surface: A stage show built around one enormous illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic and huge are synonyms, both meaning extremely large in size.

clue.text: Measure heart, taking time

indicators.note: 'taking' means the first word takes the second into its middle

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor checks a patient's heart, taking time over the measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure heart' reads like a medical instruction, but 'Measure' is the definition: a unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a metric unit of length, so it is a measure.

clue.text: Bully taking gin back from drunk concierge

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so what remains is jumbled
'taking back from' means withdrawing some letters out of the word that follows
taking something back from a place removes it, so those letters come out

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel guest snatches the gin back from a tipsy concierge, and then pushes him around.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G, I and N from CONCIERGE to leave COCERE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce someone is to force them by threats or pressure, which is what bullying does.

clue.text: Back end awfully sore

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the following letters are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient complains that their lower back is terribly painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the body, which suits the sore end; it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to back it, giving public support or approval.

clue.text: Filling for calamari: cottage cheese

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: runs across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A menu suggests stuffing squid with cottage cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cottage cheese' looks like the definition, but the answer is hidden in calamaRI COTTAge, with 'cheese' alone defining it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft, mild Italian whey cheese often used as a filling in pasta and pastries.

clue.text: Top tract of land rejected for clearance

parts.note: the head is the top of something

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for the land is read the other way round

parts.note: a moor is a tract of open upland

explanation.surface: A top piece of land is turned down for clearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearance' suggests land clearance, but it means the space above a vehicle or person.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the clear vertical space above, such as under a bridge or ceiling, so it is clearance.

clue.text: Goes on and on (in short dress!)

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the garment word loses its last letter
'in' places the small word inside the shortened garment

parts.note: dress with its final letter docked
the second appearance of this little word, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rambles on endlessly, perhaps about wearing a short dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes on and on' looks like the whole definition, but the second 'on' is wordplay, going inside a cut-short DRES.
explanation.definitionFit: To drone is to talk tediously in a monotone, so someone who drones goes on at length.

clue.text: More paintings returned by former husband

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for paintings runs backwards

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: After a divorce, more pictures are handed back by the ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional or further, so more of something is extra.

clue.text: Crowd hoot wildly for time traveller

indicators.note: wildly means without control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: nine letters of fodder taken together

explanation.surface: Fans cheer and hoot wildly at the arrival of a sci-fi hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a long-running BBC television series whose hero travels through time in the TARDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor of the BBC series journeys through time and space, the best-known fictional time traveller.

clue.text: Arab uprising very soon

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the phrase is reversed

parts.note: 'in a mo' is British slang for very soon, in a moment

explanation.surface: An Arab uprising is predicted to break out any moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a person from Oman, an Arab country on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Keeper's dog eats rodent and duck

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so the dog word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a rat is a rodent
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's dog devours a rat and a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the keeper of a museum or gallery collection, responsible for its care.

clue.text: The matter here oddly refers to oil producer

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in the odd-numbered positions: first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: odd letters of the phrase run together

explanation.surface: A formal note that the issue at hand concerns an oil company.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian tea tree yields an aromatic essential oil used as an antiseptic, so it produces oil.

clue.text: Hidden sign for office staff

parts.note: something hidden is secret
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A concealed signal meant for the office workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it simply means secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretaries are office workers who handle correspondence, records and appointments.
